scope: Bounded source-to-consumer review of ISO 32000-2:2020 §7.11.3 Table 43 and §7.11.4.1 Tables 44–45: F/UF/EF/RF/Desc/AFRelationship and embedded stream parameters Size/CreationDate/ModDate/CheckSum. This is not a whole-clause certification and does not re-audit the existing indirect-value, filtered-checksum, XFA, or associated-file tests.

source_and_errata.locator: Table 43 begins physical p.149 / printed p.134 and continues through physical p.152 / printed p.137. Table 44 is physical p.153 / printed p.138. Table 45 begins physical p.153 / printed p.138 and continues to physical p.154 / printed p.139.
effective_points: Table 43 F is the byte-string file specification. UF is the Unicode text-string alternative; when present, a PDF reader shall use UF instead of F. If EF has entries for these names, the streams are the corresponding embedded files.

EF is required if RF is present; EF values are embedded-file streams for corresponding F/UF entries. Presence of EF requires a Type entry and an indirect FileSpec. RF is optional, but each RF key must also appear in EF and its value is a related-files array. These are producer-side structural conditions; this review does not infer a reader rejection mandate.

Desc is optional descriptive text and shall be used for FileSpecs referenced by the EmbeddedFiles name tree. AFRelationship is optional, defaults to Unspecified, and names the semantic relation. NOTE 3 says it supplies no processing instructions.

Table 44: EmbeddedFile Type is optional (if present, EmbeddedFile); Subtype is optional except where required for an associated file; Params is optional except where required for an associated file. A stream is included through EF (or RF relation) and embedded content need not be directly processed by every processor.

Table 45: Size is optional and states the uncompressed embedded-file byte count; CreationDate is optional; ModDate is optional generally but required when the file is associated; CheckSum is an optional 16-byte MD5 of the uncompressed embedded-file bytes. The table note says it is a checksum, not a security mechanism. These requirements constrain producers; no blanket invalid-file rejection is inferred.
effective_errata: EC3 #155, attached to Table 44 Subtype at physical p.153 / printed p.138, narrows the producer MIME subtype form to the RFC 2046 section 2 top-level type and description separated by slash and without MIME parameters. It is not a reader filter obligation.

EC3 #481 at physical p.153 / printed p.138 replaces the earlier inclusion text: embedded streams are included only through FileSpecs with EF; name-tree embedding is optional unless another provision requires it. #156 adds associated-file and RichMedia routes. Neither changes Table 43 UF preference or Table 45 digest semantics.
EC3 #382 at physical p.154 / printed p.139 changes the CheckSum type to byte string; this preserves the 16-byte MD5 rule.

EC3 #598 at physical p.154 / printed p.139 adds NOTE 2 that CreationDate and ModDate are intended to reflect host filesystem dates when embedded, if supported by that filesystem. It does not require a reader to synthesize missing dates or access the host filesystem.
source_and_errata.annotation_check: Direct pikepdf inspection of the primary PDF's annotation dictionaries confirms #155, #156, #481, #382, and #598 at the physical pages above. #481 has a replacement annotation and the source text at the replacement location was read; it makes the old name-tree-only insertion rule obsolete. No annotation is being treated as effective solely because its ID is mentioned in the ledger.

source_and_errata.ledger: §7.11.3 and §7.11.4.1 are implemented. The current `indirect_file_parameters_spec_audit.rs` exercises direct/indirect nested values through public `attachment::attachments`, including F/UF strings, AFRelationship, EF/Params dictionaries, Type/Subtype, Size/dates/CheckSum, and literal decoded bytes. `attachment::attachments` tests are complemented by `file_specifications_audit.rs`, `associated_file_examples_audit.rs`, `embedded_files_spec_audit.rs`, and `attachments_filed.rs`.
source_and_errata.code: `crates/pdf-model/src/file_spec.rs::FileSpec::from_dictionary/display_name` reads the FileSpec and prefers UF for displayed name. `crates/pdf-model/src/attachment.rs::read` resolves EF; it selects the EF key in UF, F, DOS, Mac, Unix order, then reads stream Subtype and Params Size/dates/CheckSum. `Attachment::checksum_matches` checks decoded/uncompressed bytes; the extraction consumer's check was added under ADR 0145. `attachment::related` reads RF pairs but has no general extraction consumer.
test_coverage: T88 / indirect_file_parameters_spec_audit.rs passes the nested direct/indirect representation check and independently asserts literal payload, metadata, and digest through the attachment-listing consumer. Its indirect EF target uses F only, so it does not test competing F and UF entries.

The filtered-stream checksum control is already passing (2038-T62, combined-wave43c.log): 19 literal decoded bytes differ from the 27 Flate bytes, and the expected MD5 matches the decoded bytes only. Do not duplicate this case.

Existing file-specification tests establish UF-first display name and separate raw F bytes, not that the selected EF payload matches the UF entry when the EF dictionary has different F and UF streams.

Existing attachment writer, XFA attachment, and associated-file tests cover their own routes and fields; they do not establish a new requirement to process AFRelationship as an instruction or to extract RF files.
source_and_errata.candidate_gap: A narrow public-consumer assertion appears absent: a valid FileSpec supplies both F and UF and has distinct corresponding EF/F and EF/UF streams; the reader shall select the UF representation when present, yielding the UF name and its matching literal payload. A F-only control should prove fallback still selects the F payload. The current implementation's UF-first key ordering appears correct by inspection; this is a gap, not an observed implementation failure.

limits: No assertion here requires host file access, URL fetch, or cache behavior. Table 43 /V true prohibits caching, but the current viewer does not fetch external files; that branch has no applicable cache consumer in this scope.

The Table43 RF/EF indirection and RF pairing have existing tests. This review does not require an attachment panel to expose all related files: the current reader parses RF arrays, while ADR 0145 states there is no current extraction request/consumer for them.

Table45's conditional ModDate and EC3 #598 filesystem-date note are producer/host constraints. Existing tests carry date strings; this shard does not treat absent dates or inaccessible filesystem dates as grounds to reject a PDF.

The candidate test is not executed here. It checks only public model listing, chosen attachment name, and chosen decoded bytes; it does not certify UI rendering, native attachment handling, output writing, or all platform filename behavior.
